Replay 2026-10-25 (agent, findings in session scratchpad i124-findings.md): sink and tier are right; the 68060 class gets 44100/1024 by design (ahi_cfg.c), 28150/4096 is the 68020 class only. Underruns come from decode slower than realtime on the 060: 10 s of selecta-test.mod takes 23.9 s at 44100 with --output null (0.42x), 15.6 s at 28150 (0.64x); resampler is about 13% of it. Sink uses WaitIO (65 ms waited in 27.8 s), no busy wait. NEXT: profile which replayer claims .mod on the Amiga and its cost (nuade vs kplayer vs openmpt). Diagnostic pump_ms/STAT_AHI_DECODE_MS/STAT_AHI_WAIT_MS patch is uncommitted in render.c, tags.def, ahi_out.c. | Replay 060 2026-10-25 ($S/i124-replayer.md): the 0.42x decode was nuade on selecta-test.mod, which has no M.K. magic so kplayer rejects it; M.K. files go to kplayer on the Paula hardware route (no CPU mixing, realtime). Underruns apply only to modules kplayer cannot claim (15-sample, non-M.K. magics). Retest with an M.K. module; selection order bug logged as I293.

| I217 | [x] | - | Selecta raised recoverable alert #00080000 (AG_BadParm) at every start on the Replay 68060 (KS 47.111), even on `--output bogus`. Cause: `ahi_present()` in `src/core/amiga/machine.c` opened `ahi.device` with a 48-byte IOStdReq; AHI needs an 80-byte AHIRequest with `ahir_Version` at offset 48. Measured with a probe on the Replay: 48 bytes gives open -1 plus the alert, 80 bytes with version 4 gives open 0 and no alert. The probe therefore also reported no AHI on real hardware. Fix: `ahi_request_create` allocates 80 bytes and sets the version; sentinel `sel_machine_ahi_request` prints `ahi.request=80/4` in `selecta-cli machine`; T50 vamos test checks it (fails with 48/4 when the size is reverted). Verified on the Replay: no alert, `AUDIO=paula,ahi`. |
| I218 | [x] | - | Arrow keys did nothing in Selecta on the Replay; other keys worked (Johan, 2026-10-24). Cause: the Amiga console.device sends keys after the 8-bit CSI 0x9B (Up is 9B 41), and `plugins/ui/text/keys.c` only knew ESC [, so 0x9B became U+FFFD and the final byte a letter. Fix: 0x9B starts a CSI in the Amiga console dialect: arrows, Shift+arrows (T, S, space A, space @), F1..F10 (0~..9~, Shift 10~..19~), PC keys (Insert 40~, Page Up 41~, Page Down 42~, Home 44~, End 45~, Shift 50~..55~); Help (?~) is dropped. Tests: grid-unit decoder cases; amiga-console-keys-vamos drives the Amiga Selecta with the raw bytes (view_cursor==1); both fail with the fix reverted. Johan confirmed it works through UP-Term (2026-10-24); the native Replay keyboard and console path is still to confirm. |
| I218a | [x] | - | Amiga console text input is ISO-8859-1 (a-umlaut arrives as one byte 0xE4), but `keys.c` decodes bytes above 0x7F as UTF-8, so a non-ASCII letter typed on the Amiga swallows the next bytes. Decide the Amiga input charset path (Latin-1 to code point when the console is the Amiga console) and test it through the Amiga Selecta. Also: Del (0x7F) and Backspace (0x08) both map to Backspace on the Amiga console. Done 2026-10-24: each terminal backend declares txt_term_amiga_console; the key decoder then reads Latin-1, 0x08 Backspace and 0x7F Del, and the grid flushes Latin-1 (? above U+00FF). grid-unit and amiga-console-keys-vamos (view_cursor==3 after a 0xE4 byte) fail with the fix reverted. |

## Open decisions
Round 5 picks decided 2026-10-22 (AskUserQuestion, two calls): in = F19, F20, F21, F23, F24, F25, F29, F30, F31, F33 to F41, F43 to F46, F48, F49; restored into scope = F50 multi-zone sync, F51 server transcoding, F52 multi-user/multi-library; not picked = F32 CD audio, F42 rippers, F47 device sync; still out = Atmos, mpd client messaging, Tidal/Qobuz. Recorded in design doc sections 1a and 16. Open: none.
- [x] D-M2-1 (default taken, Q35, plan 2026-10-24-m2-amiga.md): nuade's voice API is float/double, so a nuade player ticking under a CIA interrupt on a 68020 without FPU runs soft-float in the interrupt (rule 4). Options for M2: tick in a high-priority task, upstream an integer voice API to emoon/nuade, or require an FPU for Paula-direct nuade. Source: thoughts/shared/research/2026-10-23_nuade-adapter.md. Not blocking M0b.
- [x] D-M2-2 (default taken, Q36): plain M.K. .mod on the Amiga. No nuade player probes M.K. (R8) and libopenmpt stays desktop-only in M1.1. Options for M2: a nuade M.K. player upstream (author is a friend of the user) or the UADE-native plugin. Decide at M2 planning.
- [x] D-M4-1 (Johan, 2026-10-24, AskUserQuestion): M3 finishes first (I202 green, I203 confirmed), then the M4 plan is written. No M4 code before that.
- [x] D-M4-2 (Johan, 2026-10-24): M4 leads with the most modern Amiga UI possible, built to modern UI standards from the references in the design doc (modern players are the bar), and the other Amiga UIs (MUI, GadTools, ReAction) are downscaled from it afterwards. M4 adds a new UI plugin not in the design doc: a hardware-banging custom UI, one variant for AGA (direct chipset, copper/blitter, maximum speed and fast graphics content) and one for RTG. Total custom, no toolkit limits. The M4 plan must add it to design doc sections 1a and 14.
- [x] D-M4-3 (Johan, 2026-10-24): every Amiga UI, Workbench window UIs included, opens using the full screen area by default (modern players are big; use all available screen space). Each UI also offers switchable compact modes for when Selecta should not cover the whole screen. The M4 plan specifies the compact modes and how to switch between them. The text UI already fills the window it gets once I218c lands.
- [x] D-M4-4 (Johan, 2026-10-24, AskUserQuestion): amends D-M4-1. The M4 Amiga UI plan may be written now, in parallel with the end of M3; still no M4 code before M3 finishes (I202 green, I203 confirmed). Plan file: thoughts/shared/plans/2026-10-24-m4-amiga-ui.md.
- [x] D-M4-5 (Johan, 2026-10-24, AskUserQuestion): the Mac desktop UI (SDL2, design D5) is built before the custom Amiga UI, in a new milestone after M3 (moved out of M5), so both UIs look the same. M4 toolkit UIs (MUI, ReAction, GadTools) do not wait for it; the custom Amiga UI does.
- [x] D-M4-6 (Johan, 2026-10-24, AskUserQuestion): one widget set, layout and token layer in C with three backends: SDL (desktop), RTG and AGA (Amiga). Same look by construction. Design direction: modern streaming-app look, Spotify as the reference; Johan rejected the Chipmachine two-screen layout as "cheesy retro" (M4 plan Q20). Other M4 plan answers are in its section 8a. Open: revise M4 plan sections 3, 4, 6 and the design doc milestones (section 14) to match.
- [x] D-I199-1 (Johan, 2026-10-26, AskUserQuestion): the I199 rig assertion reads the existing `fetches=` and `mirror_tries=` counters from an Execute-script redirect of `--stats` to RAM: (fetches=1, mirror_tries>=1). No new mirror_fetches counter, no core change. The mirror route is reached with SELECTA_DEVILBOX_URL=http://devilbox.uprough.net, SELECTA_NET_MAP=devilbox.uprough.net=http://127.0.0.1:<port>, SELECTA_NET_ALLOW=127.0.0.1.
Protocol additions from M1d are already in design doc section 3 (not a decision, engine protocol detail).

POST /api/auth/login {username,password} -> {token,user} (server/src/routes/auth.ts:83), JWT 30 days, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` (server/src/middleware). Live: login answers 400 on an empty body, so the route is deployed. Unblocks I173 under D-M3-12 as written.
- Hip vote exists since DEViLBOX 704a7b4eb (server/src/routes/hip.ts): GET /api/hip/vote?k=<32 hex device token>&m=<12 hex key>&r=0|5[&n=<name><=255>][&p=<player><=64>] and GET /api/hip/votes?m=&k=; reply text/plain "<count> <yours>\n", errors "ERR bad\n" (400), "ERR rate\n" (429). m is the audacious-uade xxhash32 key (HippoPlayer-68k thoughts/spot/voting-proposal.md:5,85). Token: random 128-bit, created on first vote, kept in prefs. Live: votes?m=a5cbd2fd4dbe answers "0 0". Answers Q69; unblocks I139a and I174.
- Ratings PUT accepts source modland or hvsc only (server/src/routes/ratings.ts:49); local songs have no remote rating.
- Loudness: no loudness endpoint. /api/analysis/lookup/<sha256> (server/src/routes/analysis.ts:23) returns DJ analysis with rmsDb, peakDb and an `extended` loudness set; POST /api/analysis/cache requires bpm > 0, so Selecta cannot write it.
- Share links: DEViLBOX web app reads only ?view= (src/App.tsx:114), ?collab=, ?room=, ?host=. No ?song= or ?playlist= deep link exists; Selecta's I180 song and playlist links open nothing in DEViLBOX today.
- nuade: C port of uade replayers, MIT, CMake target nuade::nuade. Tick players (framework owns clock + mixer) and self-rendering players (render_raw float stereo). Display hooks: position, voice_info, events, tracker_info/cells. Headers: scratchpad ext/nuade/include/nuade/*.h.
- bbmp: Python + Textual TUI; replayers are sandboxed helper processes in csrc/ plus libopenmpt/gme/sidplayfp/uade; docs/replayers.md, docs/collections.md, docs/formats.md.
- DEViLBOX API: base https://devilbox.uprough.net/api; ratings 1-5 (PUT/DELETE /api/ratings, Bearer JWT); batch GET max 200; item key = source + Modland full_path / HVSC path; genre GET /api/genre/:key (xxh32 of first 256 KB + size & 0xFFFF); songdb lookup by hash; modland and hvsc browse/search/download. No genre-list or artist endpoint.
- uprough-uade: UADE score.s host + real Eagleplayer/DeliTracker 68k binaries natively, Paula direct, no mixing; asm contract _music_init/start/stop/shutdown/play1/play2/set_pos/select; 40 formats on A500.
- HippoPlayer source: /Users/spot/Code/HippoPlayer-68k/code/puu016.s (playlist load 13119, header 13523, save 13542).

DESIGN 2026-11-05: (1) Manifest = TAB lines in src/library/support.c (id, file, url, size, sha256 of the download, optional cut offset/len + piece sha256, plugin, licence note); SELECTA_SUPPORT_MANIFEST replaces it (tests, mirrors). Pinned commit URLs only. (2) Storage `<cache dir>/support/<file>` (the library cache dir, outside git and the app bundle), written via .part + rename after both hashes pass. (3) Plugin/host lookup: sel_support_path(cache_dir, file, ...) returns the path only when the file exists and re-hashes to the manifest (offline, no consent needed to USE a stored file); the SEL_RP_COMPANIONS rules are per-song sibling files and do not fit a shared bank, so plugins get the path from the host. (4) Consent: pref library.support_downloads (default off), set in prefs.conf / the existing pref commands; off = no request ever. (5) Amiga: support.c is portable C on the same sel_http_request layer, but every manifest URL is https and Amiga builds are SEL_NO_TLS, so no download works there until a hippoplayer.se mirror route exists (follow-up I751b); files placed by hand in cache/support are verified the same way. Not built for Amiga in this step. FIRST CONSUMERS: default.wdb (Organya, 436212 B, github Strultz/organya.h pinned) and Beepola zx48.rom, p1d-samples.bin, svg-table-tail.bin (cut from atsidaev/beepola p1d.img/svg.img at the pinned commit, bbmp offsets/hashes re-verified). All four have stable public URLs. CLI: selecta-cli support list|get <id|all>|path <file> --cache-dir D --config-dir C; test support-dl (tests/net/support_dl.cmake). | STATUS 2026-11-06: core + CLI + test done (support-dl, red proofs: consent, whole hash, piece hash, cache use). | I787a | [x] partial | I787 | Selecta cannot open Johan's library after the I787 merge (c13fe018): SCHEMA_V13 CREATE INDEX fails with SQLITE_NOMEM (7 "out of memory", logged on a copy; Johan's DB stays v12, the same SQL takes 0.9 s in sqlite3). Cause: the sorter budget mxPmaSize = cache_size * pgsz (cache_size = g_page_slots, src/library/db/db.c set_cache_size) is page-cache memory, but the sorter allocates aMemory from the memsys5 heap part (5/8 of the block) and grows it by doubling realloc: on the 32 MiB tier 8 MiB + 16 MiB live at once > ~20 MiB heap part. Any big sort (CREATE INDEX, GROUP BY / ORDER BY without an index) hits it on every tier; on the small tier mnPmaSize (szPma 250 pages = 1 MiB) is already above the heap part. Fix at the heap config (db.c heap_configure): the sorter budgets from the memsys5 heap it allocates from (SQLITE_CONFIG_SMALL_MALLOC list sorter + soft heap limit so it flushes on nearlyFull + SQLITE_CONFIG_PMASZ scaled to the heap part); migration errors go to the log with sqlite3_errmsg. | Regression test: a v12 DB with enough rows to overflow the sorter on a small tier migrates to v13 through sel_library_open (red before, green after); Johan's DB copy opens. Done, merged to main (branch worktree-agent-ad70dd442515a513a, e14ff7b0): real cause was SQLITE_TEMP_STORE=3, which disables sorter spilling (mxPmaSize stays 0), so SMALL_MALLOC/PMASZ/soft limit alone could not help. LICENCE decision by file count in emu/cores: 33 BSD-3, 10 GPL-2.0+, 1 GPL-2.0, 6 LGPL-2.1+, 2 MIT. GPL cores are linked in, so the plugin is GPL: a separate MODULE under -DSELECTA_GPL_PLUGINS=ON with its own LICENSE; Selecta core stays MIT. PRIORITY gme vs libvgm for .vgm: libvgm owns it. Reason: Selecta's gme is built without the VGM emulator (I862), so gme cannot play .vgm/.vgz and no longer claims them; libvgm has the real chip cores and bbmp uses it for backend vgm. libvgm priority 10 also outranks gme (0) on .gym, intended since libvgm has a GYM engine with YM2612 and PSG cores. ROOT CAUSE of first silent render: PlayerA::Stop() tears down the VGM device tree (_devCfgs, _devices cleared), so Stop() before Start() played zeros while state read PLAY; shim no longer calls Stop() before Start(). (1) snsf9x/Snes9x: Snes9x licence = non-commercial only, charging money counts as commercial; not GPL, not open source; EXCLUDED. (2) SPC-only cores (blargg snes_spc LGPL, already in third_party/gme Spc_Emu): licence fine but emulate only SPC700+DSP; SNSF carries a 65816 program ROM, so cannot play SNSF. (3) bsnes/higan: GPL-3.0-or-later, usable as GPL plugin behind SELECTA_GPL_PLUGINS, Amiga exempt (GPL gate); no ready SNSF-on-bsnes glue found, needs headless ROM-in-memory boot + DSP capture + SNSF reserved/SRAM handling + psflib lib loading (SEL_RP_COMPANIONS). (4) ares sfc core: ISC (permissive; sfc-core-specific licence file unchecked), but C++17 nall, big; Amiga build unlikely. (5) psflib-based cores: psflib is only the container loader (vendored, third_party/psflib), no SNES core. Recommended: bsnes GPL plugin, est. large (new core vendoring + glue + real Modland fixture). DECISION Johan 2026-11-05: bsnes GPL-3.0 plugin (snsf9x rejected: non-commercial). Build as GPL plugin like qsf, Amiga exempt by GPL gate, real Modland fixture. | I526 | [ ] | I468 | Text on the 640x256 AGA desktop is too small to read: Johan, 2026-10-27: "the texts are too small to be really readable". The layout is drawn at ui_logical 1024x819 and scaled down to the screen, so baked glyphs shrink below a readable size. Text must be readable at its native pixel size on 640x256 (font sizes chosen for the screen, layout fitting a smaller logical size), not scaled down. Decision (Johan, 2026-10-27): 640x256 screens use bitmap fonts; the font is a bundled pixel font baked into the binary (2-3 sizes, drawn for the 2:1 tall pixels, like topaz 8), not the system font via diskfont. Text is drawn at native screen pixels, so the layout must lay out at 640x256 natively instead of drawing at 1024x819 and scaling down. Fonts (Johan, 2026-10-27: "one 8x8 and one mini", "hippoplayer has a minifont bundled that we could mimic"): two bundled bitmap fonts, an 8x8 for normal text and a mini font for dense rows, the mini drawn in the style of HippoPlayer's mini font. That font is mini4.font (sizes 6 and 8, loaded through OpenDiskFont, see HippoPlayer-68k code/puu016.s mini_text_attr; copies in HippoPlayer-68k/a1200-test/Fonts/mini4). It is a separate disk font, not covered by HippoPlayer's MIT licence, so we draw our own glyphs in its style instead of copying its bitmaps. Reference set from Johan, 2026-10-27: /Volumes/home/fonts holds mini4 (4x6, 4x8), mini6 (6x6, 6x8) and mini8 (8x8), all fixed width, chars 32-255, FPF_DESIGNED, no author or licence string in the files. Decision (Johan, 2026-10-27): ship these bitmaps as they are ("old public domain fonts ... it's fine"); this replaces the earlier draw-our-own note. Use all three families, mini4, mini6 and mini8, baked into the binary and loaded at native pixels; which family each UI role uses is part of the I526 plan. Headlines (Johan, 2026-10-27, for the 640x256 UI: "we need bitmap fonts for the headlines as well... fonts of varying sizes"): two headline sizes, a page title of about 16 rows and a section heading of about 11 rows, baked at build time from Inter SemiBold (the Mac desktop font, plugins/ui/desktop/CMakeLists.txt, gui_fontbake) at native 640x256 pixels with 2:1 tall-pixel correction and antialiased edges drawn from index8 palette shades. Body and list text use mini8, mini6 and mini4. | Johan reads every label on Home and Library on rig 2 without effort | Plan approved 2026-10-27 (thoughts/shared/plans/2026-10-27-aga-native-fonts.md, D1-D6 as recommended, 3b15886). P3-P5 agent started 2026-10-27 in the same worktree, host tests only; report i526-p3-p5-report.md. Rig 2 check after I532 frees the rig. Process sample: main > send_line > sel_engine_pump > cmd_COMPOSERS_SHOW > sel_library_composer_list > sel_genre_call > pthread_cond_wait, while the library worker runs sqlite3_step. Root cause 1 (library layer): sel_library_composer_list (src/library/db/songdb.c:389) fetches one composer per request, and op_composer_list (songdb.c ~181) re-runs the full GROUP BY over song_composers with LIMIT 1 OFFSET n each time; about 3.0 s per row on the live DB (516,675 songs, 21,817 composers), so quadratic, hours in total. Fix: one pass (one query streamed through the sink, or keyset paging), not per-row OFFSET. Root cause 2 (engine): engine commands run on the UI thread and wait synchronously on library requests; check design doc section on the library thread for whether such list queries must be async. | I595 | [x] | - | 2026-10-28, Johan: AGA/INDEX8: anti-aliased edges of UI shapes over album art (blue play button on covers) look hard and off-colour. Cause (src/gui/draw/gui_draw.c put/cube_index): the button draws in SEL_GUI_RGN_UI, so the blend of button colour and cover pixel maps through the UI cube (c->cube), whose entries hold no cover colours. Fix at root: when a partial-alpha pixel lands on an index inside an art region band (g_rgn_base/g_rgn_size), map the blend through that band's rcube so the edge picks the nearest real cover colour; mark the pen used in that region. 2026-10-28 Johan: all buttons drawn over copper gradient backgrounds look bad too. Second cause: a copper pen is one index whose real colour changes per row (copper_rgb(key, y), gui_draw.c:988), but put() blends against c->palette[*p], the pen's single stored value. Fix: when the destination index is a live copper pen, blend against copper_rgb for that row, then map to the nearest static entry. Key = 48 bits hex: hex(XXH32 of the first 256 KB of the decompressed file) + hex(filesize & 0xFFFF). Row = key, first subsong, then one 'ms,flags' entry per subsong (README.md line 64 onward documents the flags). modinfos.tsv and metadata.tsv (authors/album/year, 380k) sit beside it. Selecta's existing xxh32 key (S9) must be checked against this exact key shape. Lead from code: library queries run through sel_library_run (src/engine/engine.c run_search), which waits for the library worker, and browse_to lists synchronously; if the engine pump runs on the UI thread, every drill-down blocks painting. To do: confirm with a sample of the live app taken during the clicks, then move the query off the UI path the way LIBRARY_SYNC and search do (sel_library_task_start + collect in the pump), keep the old page visible with a loading state; regression test: a live-loop drill-down with a slowed query keeps turn_ms_max low. Sample 2026-10-31 (45 s of the live pid during Johan's clicks): the UI thread never waits on a query (sel_library_run, browse_to, sqlite3_step: 0 main-thread samples); it paints (full-frame CPU repaint plus a full SDL_UpdateTexture upload each frame, covers and gradients redrawn). The real cost is on the library worker: 19137 of 35433 samples in sel_library_items_op > sel_db_majority_format_cached > sel_db_majority_format (src/library/db/items.c:176), 18001 of them in sqlite3_step. Every list row computes its majority format by scanning all its songs (a SOURCE row scans every Modland song via `SELECT path FROM songs WHERE source=?1`), and the cache is stamped with sqlite3_total_changes64, so any DB write (history, pin, browse cache) empties it and the next items reply rescans. The page reply queues behind it, which is the freeze. Fix at the library level: keep the majority format as a stored aggregate per item (updated where songs are written, e.g. sync and pin), or key the cache on a per-source generation instead of total_changes; the items reply must not scan songs. Regression test: a host library test over a large source counts majority scans (sentinel) per items call after an unrelated write, expect 0. Second, smaller item: cache covers and gradients and upload dirty regions only (paint cost, not the freeze). On main c5ed27c0 (feature ef0aaf5d): item_formats table, schema 15; Sources reply 2628 ms to 0.8 ms on a copy of the real db, after an unrelated write 311 ms to 0.3 ms; first open after upgrade fills it once (5.7 s cold). | I694p | [ ] | Web (inside Mac track, D-WEB-3) | Krakatoa in the web build (Johan 2026-11-10: "can it be a straight canvas port for 1:1 visuals? krakatoa can use the orginal js krakatoa for web maybe? or is our port faster on the web?"). Facts: the Mac backend is an SDL_GPU compute shader (plugins/viz/krakatoa/sdl/krk_smoke_gpu.c, shaders/krk_smoke.comp); WebGL2 has no compute shaders, so it runs in a browser only through WebGPU (SDL3 WebGPU backend state UNVERIFIED; I694a spike must report it). The original is WebGL2 fragment-shader code and runs in every current browser at the same GPU cost. Options: (1) embed the original WebGL2 simulation behind the viz plugin interface, fed by Selecta audio features and the I1052c palettes; permission granted (Johan 2026-11-10 verbatim: "we have permission its a friend of mine"); repo pagustafsson/krakatoa stays private, so the web build needs a credit and a licence line agreed with the author before the public URL (I694l); (2) WebGPU path of the Mac backend where available; (3) CPU fixed-point core krk_lava_fx as fallback (low resolution). Decide after I694a. I694a finding 2026-11-10: SDL 3.2.22 (Emscripten port) has no WebGPU backend in src/gpu (d3d12, metal, vulkan only), so krk_smoke_gpu.c cannot run on the web as is; newer upstream SDL unchecked. DECIDED 2026-11-10 (Johan: "Embed original WebGL2"): option (1); credit and licence line agreed with the author before the public URL (I694l). |

| I847 | [x] | I829, I845 | Design (Opus): the interactive path. Johan 2026-10-31: "hippoplayer on the amiga puts selecta to shame searching modland etc... this is not acceptable we must have a fundamentally flawed design"; decision: design first, I846 held. Measured flaw: every library read and write (search, lists, Modland sync scan_batch commits, home items) runs on one worker thread over one SQLite connection (src/library/db/worker.c, db.c:175 NOMUTEX), and UI calls wait on it synchronously (I829), so interactive reads queue behind bulk writes; the FTS5 index (schema.c:41) itself is not the problem. Design must cover: UI never waits (I829 result); separate read connection(s) in WAL so reads never queue behind writes; bulk writes in small chunks that yield; per-platform budgets (Amiga limits only on Amiga); an interaction budget table (search-as-you-type under 100 ms on 614 000 songs, list switch under 100 ms, first paint of any page under 50 ms) with a perf test per budget on a generated 600 000-song db; how HippoPlayer searches Modland (measure, as the bar). | I848 | [ ] | I829 | Mac: double-clicking a song shows the beach ball for a while before it plays (Johan 2026-10-31: "it should show progress downloading instead not block the ui"). Expected: the click returns at once, the row or the now-playing bar shows download progress, playback starts when the file is in. Suspect: PLAY_QUERY / VIEW_ACTIVATE and the remote fetch run synchronously on the pump (I829 left them synchronous). Needs: a sample during the freeze to confirm, then a test through the real shell with a delayed fixture download that asserts the pump never waits more than 50 ms and a progress value moves. Root cause found 2026-10-31 (sample during Johan's beach ball, scratchpad sample-I848.txt): no download involved. Main thread: sel_engine_pump > cmd_OPEN > begin_song > prepare_slot > sel_library_best_source > sel_library_request, waiting on the library worker, which runs SEL_BEST_SOURCE (src/library/db/duplicates.c:228: md5 = (SELECT md5 ...) ORDER BY rank, id). songs has no md5 index, so EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN says SCAN songs: 5.9 s cold on the real db (644 327 songs, 61 444 with md5). The query at duplicates.c:166 (key = ?1 OR source=local AND path = ?1) also scans every local row (no path index). Fix: schema migration adding a partial index on songs(md5) WHERE md5 <> '' (and songs(source, path) if the plan still scans), plus a regression test asserting the plan uses the index and the open path stays under budget on a generated large db. Second half: the play path must not wait on the library at all (post and continue, as I829 does for reads); progress for remote downloads follows that. I848a merged (b1ccd7a7, schema v16: songs_md5 partial index, songs_source_path): best-source 3.497 s to 0.003 s on a copy of the real db; test library-best-source-plan (red proven for md5 only; the path-branch assertion is verified green only). The v15 to v16 migration took about 10 s once on the copy. Open: I848b, the play path posts and continues instead of waiting on the library (after I829), with download progress; hash_next (duplicates.c, called from hash_for_open on OPEN of a remote song with an md5) still scans local rows, so fix it in I848b. |

Only col_kind_play (big Play button) queues the rest. Fix level: engine play-context command (list + start index), desktop sites call it; queue-row plays start the queue index. Decided by Johan 2026-11-02: (1) Spotify context: a row click plays from that row and continues through the rest of that list; the list is the play context; songs the user added (Add to Queue / Play Next) still play first. (2) Search result click continues through the following results in order. Plan: Opus design (engine play-context: list + start index, interaction with queue, shuffle/repeat, PREV), then sonnet build; one dui reachability test: click row 3 of an album, song ends, row 4 starts. Next Mac slot, ahead of I906h. |

Agent shot 2026-11-10 (player stopped, window size, ~/Desktop/selecta-shots/I1245-viz-1.png..zoomB-x3.png): no diagonal stripes, stride shear or 3D-sampling steps found; only a faint regular 2-3 px dot grid in dark low-density areas (dither or texture quantisation). Not reproduced yet; needs Johan conditions (playing? full screen? which frames). Cause not yet known (candidates: readback row pitch, raymarch step banding without jitter, grid aliasing in upscale). Fix root cause in krk_smoke_gpu.c / krk_smoke.comp; regression test on the rendered frame (pattern metric) with revert proof. Johan (AskUserQuestion 2026-11-10): the lines are the faint dot grid. Root cause (measured): the march pass also did bloom, tone map, vignette and dither at half the surface size, and krakatoa.c scaled the result 2x2 nearest-neighbour, so each dither sample became a 2x2 block (4x4 on Retina); frame dump showed 100% equal pixel pairs at one x parity. Fix: march writes linear HDR at half size into an hdr buffer; new FINAL pass per surface pixel (bilinear upscale, bloom, tone map, vignette, PCG dither /96) as the reference's swapchain pass (design row L19); krakatoa.c copies rows 1:1. Readback grows to sw*sh*4 (~3.5 MB per frame at 1232x704). Regression: viz-krakatoa-reach now also checks the frame dump, equal-neighbour percent per x parity <= 60 (fix 16/16, revert fails). Embedding changes the file md5: update songs.md5 in the same job so duplicate groups (duplicates.c) stay right. Selecta fetches the index at start (cached, at most once a day, offline-safe) and (a) on a no_replayer open whose format an index plugin covers, the toast offers "Install <player>"; (b) a Plugins page in Settings lists installed, available and updatable plugins with Install / Update / Remove. At the same daily check Selecta offers "Update Selecta to <version>" (notes shown), downloads, verifies, replaces itself and relaunches; plugin updates are offered on the Plugins page and with the app update when the new app needs a new plugin ABI (app and plugins update together, never a loaded plugin with a mismatched ABI).
